note.note:
History:
- Chief complaint: Painful urination (stinging dysuria) for a few days (doctor summarized as 3 days).
- Associated symptoms: Mild lower abdominal cramping with urination; malodorous urine; small amount of blood in urine earlier today.
- Negatives: No urinary frequency noted; no flank/back pain; no nausea/vomiting; no fever; bowels normal without diarrhea; no vaginal discharge.
- Sexual history: Sexually active with one partner (boyfriend, ~2 months). Uses condoms. No prior STI screen.
- Menstrual history: Last period “a couple of weeks ago”; doctor restated “three weeks ago” (conflict noted).
- Pregnancy: Patient does not think she is pregnant; advised to consider a pregnancy test if concerned.

Past Medical History:
- Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).
- Allergies: Clindamycin — causes swelling (likely significant reaction).
- Medications: No regular medications. Tried over-the-counter bicarbonate for pain recently — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Family history: No known kidney, bladder, or bowel diseases.
- Social: Non-smoker. Drinks alcohol socially on weekends. College student (biology), lives with friends.

Physical Examination:
- No physical examination findings documented.
- No vital signs recorded.

Impression:
- Probable uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection (acute cystitis) without systemic features.

Management Plan:
- Antibiotics: Nitrofurantoin or Trimethoprim, one tablet twice daily for 3 days (specific agent and dose not documented).
- Hydration: Increase oral fluids to help alleviate symptoms.
- Adjuncts: Cranberry juice may help with symptoms.
- Sexual activity: Avoid intercourse until symptoms resolve; continue using condoms thereafter.
- Safety-netting: Seek care if fever develops, back/flank pain occurs, symptoms worsen, or if no improvement by the end of the week.
- Pregnancy: Take a pregnancy test if there is any concern about possible pregnancy.
- Follow-up: Call or return if symptoms persist after completing antibiotics or if red flags occur.

Patient Summary:
- 19-year-old woman with several days of stinging dysuria, mild suprapubic cramps during urination, malodorous urine, and transient hematuria; no fever, flank pain, or GI symptoms. Presentation consistent with uncomplicated cystitis.
- Empiric short-course antibiotics initiated with supportive measures and clear return precautions.

Key Takeaways:
- Start the prescribed antibiotic twice daily for 3 days and complete the course.
- Drink plenty of fluids; cranberry juice may help symptoms.
- Avoid sex until symptoms clear; return sooner for fever, back pain, or if not improving.

Next Steps:
- Monitor symptoms while on antibiotics.
- Contact clinic by the end of the week if not improved, or sooner if red-flag symptoms occur.
- Perform a pregnancy test if any concern arises.

Quality checks:
- Missing elements: No vitals recorded; no urinalysis or urine culture obtained; no pregnancy test performed; no STI screening ordered; pain severity not quantified; specific antibiotic agent and dose (mg) not documented.
- Internal conflicts: LMP reported as “a couple of weeks ago”; doctor documented “three weeks ago” (conflict noted). Symptom duration described as “a few days” vs. “last three days” (minor discrepancy).
- Transcript quality: Generally clear with minor inaudible/overlapping segments; no physical exam documented.
